scope: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part I, Chapter 5: Work, Energy and Power

objectives.text: Understand the scalar product of vectors as a mathematical prerequisite for defining work.
Define work and kinetic energy and derive the work-energy theorem for constant and variable forces.
Understand potential energy for conservative forces (gravity and springs) and the conservation of mechanical energy.
Define power and analyze elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions.

teaches.title: Scalar Product of Vectors
teaches.statement: The scalar product or dot product of any two vectors A and B, denoted as A.B, is defined as A.B = A B cos θ, where θ is the angle between the two vectors. It is a scalar quantity.

teaches.title: Work-Energy Theorem for Constant Force
teaches.statement: Starting from v^2 - u^2 = 2as, multiplying by m/2 gives 1/2 mv^2 - 1/2 mu^2 = mas = Fs. This motivates defining kinetic energy K = 1/2 mv^2 and work W = Fs, leading to Kf - Ki = W.
teaches.quote: The above equation provides a motivation for the definitions of work and kinetic energy

teaches.title: Work Done by a Constant Force
teaches.statement: Work done by a force is defined as the product of the component of the force in the direction of the displacement and the magnitude of this displacement: W = (F cos θ)d = F.d.

teaches.statement: Potential energy is 'stored' energy by virtue of the position or configuration of a body. For a conservative force F(x), potential energy V(x) is defined such that F(x) = -dV/dx.

teaches.title: Power
teaches.statement: Power is defined as the time rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. Average power Pav = W/t. Instantaneous power P = dW/dt = F.v.

notation.meaning: Scalar product of vectors A and B

conventions: The upward direction is taken as positive for gravitational potential energy calculations.
The zero of potential energy is arbitrary and chosen for convenience (e.g., ground level for gravity, equilibrium position for springs).
Friction is treated as a non-conservative force.
Collisions are analyzed assuming no external forces during the short collision time.
leaves_out: The vector product (cross product) of vectors is deferred to Chapter 6.
The three-dimensional generalization of potential energy requiring vector derivatives is outside the scope of this book.
The variation of g with height is discussed in Chapter 7 on Gravitation.
